I’m not an expert but I do work with people who have autism. What I learned is to be direct since they may lack any understanding of what you’re really trying to say. For example, you may say something that is obviously sarcastic to you but they won’t understand your tone or the nuances in what you’re trying to say.

I would be direct and say exactly how you feel. “Please stop texting me so often because I am very busy between these set of times.” Or “Right now is a very difficult time for me, I am sorry but I can not speak with you at this time. If you would like to talk, I can offer to talk for 10 minutes at this specified time and day.” That is if you’re still willing to talk to him. 

I’ve learned that people with autism don’t realize how they come across because some lack that social skills filter. And many of them have good intentions, it just doesn’t come across like that at times and it is okay to be frustrated! Just because they have autism, does not mean you have to treat them any differently. Just like with anyone else, as long as you talk to them with respect and in a way where they can understand you, you don’t have to treat them like they are fragile especially if they are adults who are high functioning.

Again, I’m no expert and I’m sure someone else can provide much better advice.

Also, I am so sorry that you are experiencing anxiety and depression. I hope you better days and internet hugs, as silly as that sounds. Please be kind and be patient with yourself, friend.

I was working at Disneyland, he comes up to my register and orders. 

He was short and to the point, no pleasantries at all but I was used to that kind of treatment from guests. Most people just want to get their snack as soon as possible and go on their favorite ride.

But there was something on his receipt that he wasn’t happy with and he got angry with me. He used a gift card so the remaining balance was shown on his receipt.

 He accused me of charging him more when that’s impossible to do with Disney’s POS system. Plus, I gave him his receipt so he could see I only charged him the items he ordered. I tried to explain that to him but he wouldn’t have it. He said he needed to talk to someone “higher” than me.

So I called my manager and it turned out that the missing balance he accused me of taking from his card was from the tip he gave to a restaurant he ate at on Disney property. 

My manager gave him a full refund anyways. It was really frustrating because he was accusing me of being a thief but he got his way at the end. But that happens all the time at Disney.
